intro-1.text: Picture this: you own Halcrest Civil Constructors, four big public jobs running, roads, a watermain, a bridge and a street rebuild. It's Monday morning.

intro-2.text: Everything about those jobs is already in TaskForce: projects, daily site reports, finance, the schedule. But one straight answer still means clicking through screens and exports.

meet-1.text: Meet TaskForce AI. You ask a question in plain English. It reads your live project records, and builds a one-page answer.

cash-ask.text: Where is our cash stuck across all our jobs, and what's the fastest way to get it back?

invoices-ask.text: Are we paying for work that never happened?

schedule-ask.text: Why is Ridgeline late, and what's it costing us?

claim-ask.text: Can we recover what the Hydro delay at Harwood has cost us?

dsr-ask.text: I want to fill today's daily site report.

cash-lead.text: First, the question every owner asks on a Monday: where is our cash stuck?

cash-point.text: {cash_total} is tied up across the four jobs. {cash_top_job} holds the most, {cash_top_job_amount}. And the fastest money back is {cash_fastest}, worth {cash_fastest_amount}.

cash-verify.text: Every figure on this page is counted from your records by code. The AI writes the words, not the numbers.

invoices-lead.text: Next, the bills. Are we paying for work that never happened?

invoices-point.text: It flagged {invoice_flag_count} invoices, with {invoice_at_risk} at risk. The biggest is {invoice_top_vendor}: {invoice_top_issue}, worth {invoice_top_amount}.

invoices-verify.text: Each invoice is checked against three sources: the subcontract, the agreed rates, and the crews your own site reports logged.

schedule-lead.text: Now the schedule. Ridgeline is running late. Why, and what is it costing us?

schedule-point.text: Ridgeline is {ridgeline_days_late} days behind. The cause is {ridgeline_cause}, and so far it has cost {ridgeline_cost}.

schedule-verify.text: To get there, it cross-checks the layers: the schedule against the daily site reports, and both against finance.

schedule-map.text: And here is where it's happening: the Ridgeline roads on the map, coloured by progress.

claim-lead.text: That Hydro delay at Harwood has a price. Can we get it back?

claim-point.text: It builds the claim: {claim_days} delay days at Harwood, worth {claim_total} in standby crews and equipment.

claim-verify.text: It only counts days the records link to the Hydro delay. The days it left out are listed, and every line points to its daily report. Where the records can't prove something, it says so instead of guessing.

dsr-lead.text: All of this starts with what your superintendents report at the end of the day. So here's Maria, at five o'clock.

dsr-open.text: The daily site report opens beside the chat. No typing, no dropdowns. She just talks.

fill-1.text: Okay, so this is my end of day report. I'm Maria Santos, and I was the site supervisor today. It was a day shift on the Ridgeline Regional Roads program, out at Payne Road. On our own crew we had our foreman, six general labourers and fourteen dump truck drivers, and everybody put in ten hours. Kestrel was paving item 109 today. Their crew was two asphalt paver operators, five asphalt rakers and four roller operators. All eleven of them worked ten hours, and every one of them, pavers, rakers and rollers, sat one hour on standby because of the rain. Lakeview delivered sixteen hundred and forty tonnes of HL3 hot mix, and we placed all sixteen hundred and forty tonnes on item 109. For equipment we ran our Caterpillar AP600F paver, our BOMAG 1055 paver, our BW213D roller and our CB10 roller, ten hours each. Then, after lunch, the rain stopped the work at two o'clock for about an hour. The one thing still stuck is Hydro. They still haven't moved the pole at the Harwood Road culvert, and that's holding up the culvert work there. But what did get done is the HL3 lift on Payne Road, from the culvert up to the north end. It's all rolled and compacted.

fill-1-point.text: The form fills itself, matched to your real records: the contract item, the sub, the material and the equipment.

fill-1-missing.text: And it notices what's missing, and asks.

fill-1-ask.text: What was the weather and temperature on site?

fill-2.text: It started overcast, about eight degrees, then rain most of the afternoon.

fill-2-point.text: The weather goes straight in. Nothing to retype.

dsr-review.text: Before it's submitted, Maria checks one clean summary, and it's done.

outro-1.text: From what your superintendents say at five o'clock, to the answers you need on Monday morning. That's TaskForce AI.
